transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main reason is I’m losing a lot of time to things that should be quick. Like I’ll read an email over and over before sending it, or even after sending it, and then I’m checking texts the same way. I’ll reopen folders on my computer to make sure I didn’t miss something or put something in the wrong place.

It’s not even always complicated stuff. I work with computers, so I know my way around files, but I can get stuck, you know? Before I leave the house or start work, I’ll replay conversations in my head, like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t say something wrong or make some serious mistake. And then suddenly a half hour is gone. Sometimes more. It’s just… it’s starting to interfere.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that you don’t want or can’t control, and that you feel you have to keep checking or thinking through to feel okay?

Yeah, yes. That’s pretty much it. I’ll be trying to focus on something normal, like working through a system design, or preparing a lesson, and this thought just barges in—like, what if I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or I mishandled some family photos, or I let someone in the community down somehow.

And I know, logically, I’ve already gone over it. I mean, I’ll tell myself, “You checked that already,” but it doesn’t really settle. It’s like I have to keep thinking through it until it feels okay, except it doesn’t always get there. Then I’m off on this whole mental detour instead of doing the thing I sat down to do.
When you have these intrusive thoughts, do you feel driven to do something — like checking, reviewing, or mentally going over things — to try to reduce the anxiety or make sure nothing bad happens?

Yes, I do. I mean, that’s kind of the thing that finally got me to come in. I’ll feel pushed to re-read an email or a text again and again, even if I know what it says. Or I’ll reopen folders on my computer to make sure I didn’t put something in the wrong place.

And it’s not always even on the computer. Before I leave the house, or before I start working, I can get stuck mentally replaying a conversation, like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t say something wrong or make some serious mistake. It reminds me a little of when I used to debug code and you’d keep tracing the same line because you’re sure there’s a flaw somewhere—except here it’s my own memory I’m debugging, I guess.

But yeah, the short answer is yes. I keep checking or reviewing because otherwise I don’t feel settled, and then big chunks of time disappear.

When you're going over things again and again, does it feel more like something you have to do to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce your anxiety, rather than something you want to do or enjoy doing?

Yeah, no, it’s definitely not something I enjoy. It feels more like I have to do it so I can be sure I didn’t mess something up.

Like, I’ll re-read an email or a text, and then I’ll think, okay, but did I miss some detail? And then I’m back in it again. Same with folders on the computer—I’ll reopen them even though I basically know what’s there. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

And before I leave the house or sit down to work, I can get caught replaying conversations in my head. Not because I want to reminisce or anything—more like I’m checking whether I said something wrong. It eats up these chunks of time, and then I look at the clock and feel ridiculous, honestly.
